blockers.statement: Capability bit 8 remains unadvertised. The live runtime-to-gem5 probe proves canonical negative hello and baseline reconnect only; it sends no MessageType 18 frame, so the positive generic socket route is unproven.

The daemon handler policy accepts only page-backed ALLOC alignments 4096 and 65536, while the normal runtime and retained Triton metadata request logical alignment 8; page size is also fixed for the owner session after the first successful MAP.

The existing v1 MEMORY_COPY_H2D carrier is not proven through a live generic daemon session, and SUBMIT, queue/signal/AQL packet ownership, packet CRC, lifecycle ticks, successful ACK, and MessageType 20 completion remain fail-closed.
The retained Triton descriptor carries 12 DWORD (48-byte) kernarg preload and preload-aware native mapping plus entry-offset semantics remain unimplemented; the image must continue to fail closed.

No normal Triton launcher, compiler/JIT transport, positive generic lifecycle, GPUDispatcher/ComputeUnit kernel execution, output differential, fallback, or Qwen inference has been demonstrated through the CP24 path.

changes: Accepted a bounded partial gem5 daemon-handler boundary: a per-client owner/generation-bound generic session, MessageType 18 dispatch branch, canonical MessageType 19 ACK plumbing, cleanup ordering, MAP/ALLOC/UNMAP native-state calls, and explicit fail-closed SUBMIT.

Added a shared generic route-policy harness covering absent-capability canonical failure, failure zeroing and no mutation, MAP/UNMAP policy, 4K/64K page rules, logical alignment-8 rejection, and SUBMIT rejection without advertising capability bit 8.

Added an opt-in runtime endpoint test. The complete runtime CTest result is 20 total, 19 passed, one expected endpoint skip, and zero failed; a separate live VEGA_X86 run proves canonical required-generic rejection and baseline reconnect with bit 8 unselected.

Preserved the existing v1 MEMORY_COPY_H2D sealed-FD carrier instead of adding a KERNARG opcode. Handler source can recognize owner-bound kernarg H2D, but no live daemon H2D path or positive allocation lifecycle is claimed.

Kept positive MessageType 18 routing, bit-8 advertisement, normal alignment 8, successful SUBMIT ACK, MessageType 20 completion, launcher, compiler/JIT, GPU execution, output correctness, and CPU/NVIDIA fallback false.
limitations: CP24 is accepted as a bounded partial handler milestone so the next transaction can proceed; accepted does not mean the CP23 target of a complete advertised daemon lifecycle was met.
The route-policy harness tests shared policy and codec helpers, not HostGPUBridge's live Unix-socket MAP/ALLOC/H2D/UNMAP route. Its raw type-18 canonical rejection is not socket proof.
The live runtime-to-gem5 evidence covers hello negotiation and baseline retry only. It sends no MessageType 18 request and leaves capability bit 8 unadvertised and unselected.
The handler accepts only 4096/65536 ALLOC alignment and fixes page size for the owner session; the normal logical alignment 8 is rejected and no positive ALLOC route is interoperable yet.
Kernarg bytes retain the existing sealed-FD v1 MEMORY_COPY_H2D carrier. Runtime mock behavior and handler source exist, but a live daemon H2D route is unproven and no KERNARG v2 opcode is introduced.

SUBMIT always fails with UnsupportedCapability; no successful SUBMIT ACK, MessageType 20 completion, queue/signal/packet CRC/tick lifecycle, cancellation after admission, or disconnect retirement is claimed.
The live gem5.opt is hash-bound but was not freshly rebuilt in full because of the known unrelated amdgpu_device.cc pointer-member build blocker outside CP24.

The retained 12-DWORD preload, normal Triton launcher, compiler/JIT, GPUDispatcher/ComputeUnit execution, output differential, timing/performance, fallback, and Qwen end-to-end remain unsupported or false.
